TIP: Any field below accepts a comma-separated list of values (e.g. 1.5,2,2.5). When more than one field has multiple values, every combination is computed and returned as a table, so you do not need to re-run this dialog for each scenario.
sd: Standard Deviation of Covariate (comma-separated for multiple values)
propevent: Proportion with the Event (0-1; comma-separated for multiple values)
hr: Hazard Ratio of Covariate (comma-separated for multiple values)

siglevel: Significance Level (0-1; comma-separated for multiple values)

help.title: Sample Size, Test Cox Model
help.body:
This is an assessment of sample size for a single covariate in a Cox proportional hazards model. It computes the sample size or power, when the user specifies the other one, given a hazard ratio to detect.

Sample Size: Specify the total number of subjects. Comma-separated lists are accepted.

Power: Specify the desired power of the study, i.e. the probability that the test will reject the null hypothesis if the alternative hypothesis was true. Comma-separated lists are accepted.

Standard Deviation of Covariate: Specify the standard deviation of the covariate pertaining to the hazard ratio. Comma-separated lists are accepted.

Hazard Ratio, Group 1 vs Group 2: Specify the desired hazard ratio to detect for the covariate. Comma-separated lists are accepted.

Proportion with the Event: Specify the expected proportion of the sample with the event (or one minus the censoring proportion). If you specify a probability of 1, it assumes no censoring. Comma-separated lists are accepted.

R-squared between the covariate and other covariates; enter 0 for unadjusted test: Specify the r-squared value (squared multiple correlation), between the covariate and all other covariates in the Cox model. A value of 0 corresponds to an anadjusted test with no other covariates. Comma-separated lists are accepted.

Significance Level: Specify the desired significance level (i.e. type I error) of the test. Comma-separated lists are accepted.

This uses the ssizeEpiCont.default and powerEpiCont.default functions in the powerSurvEpi package. See triple dot menu>Help>R Function Help for more information.

Generate Power Curve Plot: When multiple values are supplied for more than one field, check this box to plot the results. Choose which computed quantity goes on the X-axis, and optionally one or more fields to group/color separate curves by.

Required R Packages: powerSurvEpi, ggplot2
